tagline: No passing to Galena, where the old bridge forks.
intro: Branson West was Linchpin once, then Lakeview, until 1992, when it took the name of its busier neighbor. From there Route 265 heads north with Route 413 through mountainous country to Reeds Spring. Past Reeds Spring, Route 248 joins in, and the three share one winding two-lane road of switchbacks to Galena. It is striped no-passing the whole way.
At Galena the road crosses the James River and turns west, then north through farmland and woods by Elsey to Crane, and on toward the Christian County line.

moments.title: Reeds Spring
moments.text: Fitzhugh Reed settled by a spring here and farmed it as Reed's Springs before the town was organized in 1906 and kept his name.

moments.title: Y-Bridge
moments.text: The 1927 bridge over the James forks at its east end like a Y, so traffic could turn north or south between bluff and river. Cars now use a newer bridge to the north.

moments.title: Crane
moments.text: The town is named for Crane Creek, which was named for the blue cranes in the area and runs past the southwest side of town as a Blue Ribbon Trout Area.
